```{r}
#| label: load-packages-r

library(tidyverse)
library(nanoparquet)
library(nnet)

# The factor zoo of lectures 10 to 13
sample_start <- ymd("1973-01-01")
sample_end <- ymd("2023-12-31")
test_start <- ymd("2000-01-01")
n_folds <- 5
ridge_lambdas <- 10^seq(-7, -1, by = 0.25)
macro_names <- c("dp", "tbl", "tms", "dfy", "svar")
test_years <- paste0(year(test_start), "–", year(sample_end))

# The inputs and hidden units of the network for the forecasts. The slide
# "A feed-forward network" counts its parameters; the network's code on the
# slide "A network for the returns of the zoo" defines them again
features <- c("ret_lag_1", "momentum_12", macro_names)
hidden_units <- 5

months_per_year <- 12

# Colours of the slides, used by the figures
ku_red <- "#901A1E"
jet <- "#3d3d3d"
grey <- "#666666"
light <- "#e6e3df"
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

```{python}
#| label: load-packages-py
#| include: false
from datetime import date

import numpy as np
import polars as pl
from sklearn.neural_network import MLPRegressor
```

```{r}
#| label: lectures-10-to-13-code
#| include: false
# The data, the ridge SDF and the forecast panel of lectures 10 to 13
osap_url <- paste0(
  "https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenSourceAP/CrossSection/resolve/",
  "Data-Release-2026.10/Portfolios/Full%20Sets%20OP/PredictorLSretWide.parquet"
)
osap_file <- "data/osap_long_short_returns.parquet"
if (!file.exists(osap_file)) {
  download.file(osap_url, osap_file, mode = "wb")
}
anomalies <- read_parquet(osap_file) |>
  mutate(date = floor_date(as.Date(date), "month")) |>
  filter(between(date, sample_start, sample_end)) |>
  select(date, where(\(x) !anyNA(x)))
returns <- as.matrix(select(anomalies, -date)) / 100
estimation <- anomalies$date < test_start
x_estimation <- returns[estimation, ]

sharpe_ratio <- function(x) mean(x) / sd(x) * sqrt(months_per_year)
ridge_weights <- function(x, lambda) {
  solve(crossprod(x) + nrow(x) * lambda * diag(ncol(x)), colSums(x))
}
folds <- ceiling(seq_len(nrow(x_estimation)) / (nrow(x_estimation) / n_folds))
cv_sharpe <- function(fit_weights, lambda) {
  map_dbl(seq_len(n_folds), \(k) {
    weights <- fit_weights(x_estimation[folds != k, ], lambda)
    sharpe_ratio(x_estimation[folds == k, ] %*% weights)
  }) |>
    mean(na.rm = TRUE)
}
ridge_lambda <- ridge_lambdas[which.max(map_dbl(ridge_lambdas, \(lambda) {
  cv_sharpe(ridge_weights, lambda)
}))]
ridge_sharpe <- c(
  estimation = sharpe_ratio(
    returns[estimation, ] %*% ridge_weights(x_estimation, ridge_lambda)
  ),
  test = sharpe_ratio(
    returns[!estimation, ] %*% ridge_weights(x_estimation, ridge_lambda)
  )
)

macro <- read_parquet("data/macro_predictors.parquet") |>
  transmute(date = date %m+% months(1), across(all_of(macro_names))) |>
  mutate(across(all_of(macro_names), \(x) {
    (x - mean(x[date < test_start])) / sd(x[date < test_start])
  }))
panel <- anomalies |>
  pivot_longer(-date, names_to = "anomaly", values_to = "ret") |>
  mutate(ret = ret / 100) |>
  arrange(anomaly, date) |>
  mutate(
    ret_lag_1 = lag(ret),
    momentum_12 = slider::slide_dbl(
      lag(ret),
      mean,
      .before = 11,
      .complete = TRUE
    ),
    .by = anomaly
  ) |>
  left_join(macro, join_by(date)) |>
  drop_na()
train <- panel |> filter(date < test_start)
test_rows <- panel$date >= test_start

covariance <- cov(x_estimation)
forecast_row <- function(method, forecast) {
  oos_r2 <- 1 -
    sum((panel$ret[test_rows] - forecast[test_rows])^2) /
      sum(panel$ret[test_rows]^2)
  portfolio <- panel |>
    mutate(forecast = forecast) |>
    select(date, anomaly, forecast, ret) |>
    nest(data = -date) |>
    mutate(
      ret = map_dbl(data, \(d) {
        order <- match(colnames(returns), d$anomaly)
        weights <- solve(
          covariance + ridge_lambda * diag(ncol(returns)),
          d$forecast[order]
        )
        sum(weights * d$ret[order])
      })
    )
  tibble(
    method = method,
    oos_r2 = oos_r2,
    estimation = sharpe_ratio(portfolio$ret[portfolio$date < test_start]),
    test = sharpe_ratio(portfolio$ret[portfolio$date >= test_start])
  )
}
```

# Neural networks

## A feed-forward network

::: {.box}
Build a flexible function $g(z)$ from simple pieces: each **neuron** takes a weighted sum of its inputs and passes it through a nonlinear **activation**
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$
h^{(1)} = \sigma\big(W^{(1)} z + c^{(1)}\big), \quad h^{(2)} = \sigma\big(W^{(2)} h^{(1)} + c^{(2)}\big), \quad g(z) = w' h^{(L)} + c
$$

- $\sigma(x) = \max(x, 0)$ (ReLU) or the logistic function. Without $\sigma$, the network would be linear regression
- With enough neurons, a network approximates any smooth function. The price: many parameters, here `r (length(features) + 1) * hidden_units + hidden_units + 1` already for one layer of `r hidden_units` neurons and `r length(features)` inputs
:::

## Training a network

- **Loss:** the mean squared forecast error, as for OLS. No closed form: **gradient descent** moves all weights a small step against the gradient of the loss
- **Backpropagation:** the chain rule gives the gradients of all layers in one backward pass; mini-batches of observations make each step cheap
- **Regularization**, because the network can fit the noise:
  - **weight decay:** a ridge penalty on the weights
  - **early stopping:** stop when the loss in a validation sample rises; the validation sample also chooses the penalty
  - **dropout:** switch off random neurons during training
  - **ensembles:** average networks from different random starts
- Gu, Kelly & Xiu (2020) use all of them; their best networks have three or four layers

## A network for the returns of the zoo

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```{r}
#| label: network-function-r
# The predictors of lecture 13, scaled with the estimation sample
features <- c("ret_lag_1", "momentum_12", "dp", "tbl", "tms", "dfy", "svar")
scale_inputs <- function(data) {
  scale(data[features], colMeans(train[features]), map_dbl(train[features], sd))
}
ret_sd <- sd(train$ret) # returns in units of volatility give the decay a scale

hidden_units <- 5
fit_network <- function(data, decay, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  nnet(
    scale_inputs(data),
    data$ret / ret_sd,
    size = hidden_units,
    decay = decay,
    linout = TRUE,
    maxit = 500,
    trace = FALSE
  )
}
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: network-function-py
#| eval: false
# The predictors of lecture 13, scaled with the estimation sample
features = ["ret_lag_1", "momentum_12", "dp", "tbl", "tms", "dfy", "svar"]
centers = train.select(features).mean().to_numpy()
input_sd = train.select(features).std().to_numpy()
scale_inputs = lambda data: (data.select(features).to_numpy() - centers) / input_sd
ret_sd = train["ret"].std()  # returns in units of volatility give the decay a scale

hidden_units = 5


def fit_network(data, decay, seed):
    network = MLPRegressor(
        hidden_layer_sizes=(hidden_units,),
        activation="logistic",
        solver="lbfgs",
        alpha=decay,
        max_iter=500,
        random_state=seed,
    )
    return network.fit(scale_inputs(data), data["ret"].to_numpy() / ret_sd)
```
:::

## Weight decay and an ensemble

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```{r}
#| label: fit-network-r
#| cache: true
#| cache.extra: !expr list(deparse(fit_network), deparse(scale_inputs), features, hidden_units, ret_sd, nrow(panel))
# Fit until validation_start, choose the weight decay on the years after
validation_start <- ymd("1995-01-01")
decays <- c(1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000)
fitting <- filter(train, date < validation_start)
validation <- filter(train, date >= validation_start)
validation_mse <- map_dbl(decays, \(decay) {
  network <- fit_network(fitting, decay, seed = 1)
  forecast <- predict(network, scale_inputs(validation)) * ret_sd
  mean((validation$ret - forecast)^2)
})
decay <- decays[which.min(validation_mse)]

# An ensemble: the average forecast of networks from different random starts
n_networks <- 5
network_forecasts <- map(seq_len(n_networks), \(seed) {
  network <- fit_network(train, decay, seed)
  as.vector(predict(network, scale_inputs(panel))) * ret_sd
})
network_forecast <- reduce(network_forecasts, `+`) / n_networks
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: fit-network-py
#| eval: false
# Fit until validation_start, choose the weight decay on the years after
validation_start = date(1995, 1, 1)
decays = [1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000]
fitting = train.filter(pl.col("date") < validation_start)
validation = train.filter(pl.col("date") >= validation_start)
validation_mse = []
for decay in decays:
    network = fit_network(fitting, decay, seed=1)
    forecast = network.predict(scale_inputs(validation)) * ret_sd
    validation_mse.append(np.mean((validation["ret"].to_numpy() - forecast) ** 2))
decay = decays[np.argmin(validation_mse)]

# An ensemble: the average forecast of networks from different random starts
n_networks = 5
network_forecasts = [
    fit_network(train, decay, seed).predict(scale_inputs(panel)) * ret_sd
    for seed in range(1, n_networks + 1)
]
network_forecast = np.mean(network_forecasts, axis=0)
```
:::

```{r}
#| label: network-row
#| include: false
network_row <- forecast_row("Neural network", network_forecast)
ols_fit <- lm(reformulate(features, response = "ret"), data = train)
ols_row <- forecast_row("OLS", predict(ols_fit, panel))
```

## The network's forecasts

- One hidden layer of `r hidden_units` logistic neurons, weight decay `r decay` (chosen on `r year(validation_start)`–`r year(test_start) - 1`), `r n_networks` networks averaged
- Out-of-sample $R^2$ `r percent(network_row$oos_r2, 0.01)` (OLS: `r percent(ols_row$oos_r2, 0.01)`); as a portfolio with the forecasts as expected returns (lecture 13): Sharpe ratio `r number(network_row$test, 0.01)` in the test sample
- `nnet()` and scikit-learn (same penalty scale) start from different random weights, so their networks differ a little

# Learning the SDF

## SDF weights that depend on the state

::: {.box}
Lecture 11: constant weights, $m = 1 - b'(F - E[F])$; written without centring, [$M_{t+1} = 1 - b'F_{t+1}$,]{style="white-space: nowrap"} the weights are proportional to the same $\Sigma^{-1}\mu$. Now each anomaly's weight depends on what we know at $t$: $M_{t+1} = 1 - \sum_i \omega(I_{t}, z_{i,t})\, F_{i,t+1}$
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$
E\big[M_{t+1} F_{i,t+1} \mid I_t\big] = 0 \qquad \Longleftrightarrow \qquad E\big[M_{t+1} F_{i,t+1}\, g(I_t, z_{i,t})\big] = 0 \ \text{ for all } g
$$

- The conditional moments hold for every **instrument** $g$: every managed portfolio $F_{i,t+1}\, g(\cdot)$ must be priced, too
- A network $\omega(\cdot)$ for the weights, estimated by minimizing the squared pricing errors of these moments
:::

## The adversary

- Infinitely many instruments $g$: which ones should the SDF price? Chen, Pelger & Zhu (2024): let a **second network** choose them
- The adversary picks the managed portfolios with the **largest pricing errors**; the SDF network then learns to price them. A game, like a generative adversarial network:

$$
\min_{\omega} \ \max_{g} \ \frac{1}{N}\sum_i \Big\| E\big[M_{t+1} F_{i,t+1}\, g(I_t, z_{i,t})\big] \Big\|^2
$$

- Their result on US stocks: an SDF with an out-of-sample Sharpe ratio far above linear factor models, using the macro state and characteristics

## Chen–Pelger–Zhu light on the zoo

```{r}
#| label: cpz-results
#| include: false
# The search on UCloud: every setting with ensembles of nine networks
ensemble_size <- 9
cpz_results <- "lecture-slides/factor-zoo/results"
cpz_runs <- read_csv(
  file.path(cpz_results, "cpz_light_runs.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  filter(seeds == ensemble_size) |>
  mutate(
    model = if_else(
      str_detect(model, "Chen"),
      "Chen–Pelger–Zhu light",
      "Feed-forward SDF"
    )
  )
n_settings <- n_distinct(
  cpz_runs$hidden,
  cpz_runs$dropout,
  cpz_runs$weight_decay,
  cpz_runs$pcs,
  cpz_runs$no_macro
)
cpz_chosen <- cpz_runs |> slice_max(sr_valid, n = 1, by = model)
cpz_light <- cpz_chosen |> filter(model == "Chen–Pelger–Zhu light")
feed_forward <- cpz_chosen |> filter(model == "Feed-forward SDF")
cpz_correlation <- cpz_runs |>
  summarize(correlation = cor(sr_valid, sr_test), .by = model) |>
  deframe()

# The networks' returns start once every input has a year of history
cpz_start <- list.files(
  cpz_results,
  paste0("^cpz_light_sdf_returns_seeds-", ensemble_size),
  full.names = TRUE
)[1] |>
  read_parquet() |>
  pull(date) |>
  min()
validation_years <- paste0(year(validation_start), "–", year(test_start) - 1)
```

```{python}
#| label: show-cpz-networks
#| eval: false
def network(n_out, hidden, dropout):
    return nn.Sequential(
        nn.Linear(n_inputs, hidden),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Dropout(dropout),
        nn.Linear(hidden, hidden),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Dropout(dropout),
        nn.Linear(hidden, n_out),
    )


def pricing_loss(weights, instruments, months):
    """Mean squared pricing error of the moments E[M F_i g_j] = 0."""
    sdf = 1 - (weights * returns).sum(dim=1)
    priced = sdf[:, None, None] * returns[:, :, None] * instruments
    moments = priced[months].mean(dim=0)
    return (moments**2).sum(dim=1).mean()
```

- **Inputs of each anomaly:** last month's return, factor momentum, its historical mean, its loadings on the first `r max(cpz_runs$pcs)` principal components; optionally the macro state
- **Training** `r year(cpz_start)`–`r year(validation_start) - 1`, **validation** `r validation_years` (early stopping and the choice of the setting), test from `r year(test_start)`. PyTorch only: `lecture-slides/factor-zoo/cpz_light.py`, `r n_settings` settings × `r ensemble_size` networks, 2 h 14 min on 64 UCloud cores

## What the networks earn

```{r}
#| label: plot-cpz
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.3
ggplot(cpz_runs, aes(x = sr_valid, y = sr_test, color = model)) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = ridge_sharpe[["test"]],
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = grey
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = min(cpz_runs$sr_valid),
    y = ridge_sharpe[["test"]],
    label = "Ridge SDF",
    hjust = 0,
    vjust = -0.5,
    color = grey
  ) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = cpz_chosen, size = 5, shape = 21, stroke = 1.3, fill = NA) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Chen–Pelger–Zhu light" = ku_red, "Feed-forward SDF" = "#b3b3b3")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    x = paste0("Sharpe ratio, validation ", validation_years, " (annualized)"),
    y = paste0("Sharpe ratio, test ", test_years, "\n(annualized)"),
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

- Each dot is one of the `r n_settings` settings; circles: the setting chosen on the validation sample. The adversary helps: `r number(cpz_light$sr_test, 0.01)` against `r number(feed_forward$sr_test, 0.01)` without it
- For Chen–Pelger–Zhu light, the validation Sharpe ratio predicts the test Sharpe ratio (correlation `r number(cpz_correlation[["Chen–Pelger–Zhu light"]], 0.01)`). But no setting reaches the ridge SDF

## Flexibility against economic structure

- **Nagel (2021):** returns are noisy and samples are short; machine learning in asset pricing works best with economic restrictions, such as a prior that rules out implausibly high Sharpe ratios
- **Our scoreboard:** `r ncol(returns)` anomalies, `r year(test_start) - year(sample_start)` years of estimation data. The ridge SDF has one tuning parameter and an economic prior; the networks have thousands of parameters and only the data
- Gu, Kelly & Xiu and Chen, Pelger & Zhu use tens of thousands of stocks and decades of data: there, flexibility pays

::: {.highlight}
The more data, the more flexibility can pay; with little data, economic structure wins
:::

```{r}
tibble(

    "Ridge (prior on Sharpe ratios)",
    "Forecasts: OLS",

    "Feed-forward SDF",
    "Chen–Pelger–Zhu light"
  ),

  ),
  estimation = c(
    ridge_sharpe[["estimation"]],

  ),
  test = c(
    ridge_sharpe[["test"]],
    ols_row$test,
    network_row$test,
    feed_forward$sr_test,
    cpz_light$sr_test
  )
) |>
  mutate(across(c(estimation, test), \(x) number(x, 0.01))) |>
  rename(
    `Sharpe ratio, estimation` = estimation,
    !!paste("Sharpe ratio", test_years) := test
  )
```

- The SDF networks: setting chosen on the validation sample `r validation_years`, ensembles of `r ensemble_size` networks. The rows of lectures 10 to 13 stay on the scoreboard
